experiment: LLMs (Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5) with web search/fetch only, no gomisute-gps data, answering garbage-day questions in 5 municipalities whose collection calendars are published only as PDF/image (colors, icons, scans) — follow-up to llm-baseline.json (Kanazawa)

conditions.question_form: 「<住所> に住んでいます。<YYYY>年<M>月<D>日(<曜>)にはどのごみを出せますか？」, one independent agent per question and model, asked once
conditions.allowed_tools: WebSearch and WebFetch (loaded via ToolSearch). In this harness WebFetch returns only raw bytes for a PDF (tested on Murakami 74793.pdf: no legend, no dates) but saves the file locally; agents were allowed to open exactly that saved file (or a saved image) with Read, which shows PDF pages as images. No Bash, no other files, no gomisute-gps data.
conditions.audit: All Read calls in the 60 runs opened files that WebFetch had saved (tool-results/webfetch-*). Two runs also called a UI-only tool once (Z4 opus: wrap_up; O5 haiku: update_plan); this did not affect answers. WebFetch caches by URL, so runs that fetched the same URL opened the same saved file.
conditions.output: user-facing Japanese answer plus JSON {items, no_collection, district, confidence, hedged, sources, tools_used, files_opened}

ground_truth_method: For each question one reader (the experimenter, a Claude Opus 5.5 session) rendered the official PDF/image as zoomed crops (one month or table at a time, about 2–3x) and read the cell, legend and notes; a second, independent agent (Claude Opus 5.5) answered the same questions without seeing the first reading, also from the official files. All 30 questions agreed and were kept. The second reader caught one misreading by the first reader (Murakami 74793, 11/23 shaded light blue = collected) on a date that was not used as a question. Districts come from the municipality's own tables where they exist (Asahikawa HTML table, Miyazaki area PDF, Murakami r8 page lists for 荒川/神林, Tokai footnotes and 住居表示 image, Onagawa 行政区 legend); for 村上地域 (M1–M4) no official street→district list exists, so the calendar titles and the city's 2020 census table (52831.pdf) were used.

scoring.district: correct = names the collection district/pattern/area the truth uses; none = gives no district
scoring.claim_check: one fact-check agent per municipality listed every factual claim in all 12 answers (surrounding dates, year-end days, rules, bags, times, phone numbers, URLs) and checked each against the official PDFs/pages
